pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

2. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

3. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. D — newton (N)

5. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

7. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

9. D — Glucose and oxygen

10. D — 100 °C

11. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Nutrition in animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Interdependence of Life; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Curved mirrors; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
